paragraphs: Aeolus is a flight-delay dataset designed to represent both individual flights and the connections through which delays spread. Its tabular component covers more than 50 million flights, with operational, weather, and airport information. The motivation is that a flat table alone does not capture the timing and relationships involved in delay propagation.

The dataset adds two aligned views of those flights. A flight-chain component connects successive flight legs, representing dependencies between earlier and later operations. A network graph captures connections through shared aircraft, crews, and airport resources. These views let researchers examine a flight through its own attributes, its position in a sequence, and its relationships with other flights.

Aeolus uses temporal splits and explicit leakage prevention to support realistic, reproducible evaluation. It accommodates regression, classification, sequence modeling, and graph learning within one benchmark. Released baseline experiments and preprocessing tools support adoption. The contribution is a shared resource for studying whether structured relationships improve flight-delay modeling and for developing foundation models for tabular data.
neurips-2025-aeolus-a-multi-structural-f.tldr: Aeolus connects data on over 50 million flights with flight sequences and resource-sharing graphs to support structured flight-delay research.

paragraphs: Analog in-memory computing offers a route to faster, more power-efficient neural-network inference, but its calculations are noisy and its inputs and outputs have restricted precision. These properties create an accuracy problem for language models transferred directly to analog hardware. The paper develops a general, scalable training method for adapting large pretrained language models to these conditions.

The authors demonstrate the approach with Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct and Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Despite analog noise and quantization constraints, the adapted models retain performance comparable to baselines using 4-bit weights and 8-bit activations. The result addresses the combined effects of limited numerical precision and imperfect computation, both of which matter for execution on analog hardware.

The training method also produces models that can be quantized for low-precision digital inference. In addition, the adapted models benefit from additional computation at test time, with better scaling behavior than the stated baseline using 4-bit weights and static 8-bit input quantization. Together, these findings support a path toward efficient foundation models across analog and low-precision digital platforms.
neurips-2025-analog-foundation-models-a3.tldr: A scalable adaptation method helps language models retain performance under the noise and precision constraints of analog computing.

paragraphs: Group Relative Policy Optimization trains reasoning models using multiple generated answers, or completions, for each question. This can be expensive because increasing the number of completions multiplies training time. The paper's experiments and theoretical analysis show that completion count affects accuracy, while individual completions differ in how much they contribute to learning.

Completion Pruning Policy Optimization, or CPPO, uses relative advantage to identify those differences. It removes completions whose advantages have small absolute values from gradient calculations and updates. The selection therefore depends on the strength of the learning signal, including its magnitude in either direction. A second component dynamically allocates completions and brings in additional questions to improve GPU utilization.

The reported experiments achieve speedups of up to 7.98 times on GSM8K and 3.48 times on Math, while maintaining or improving accuracy relative to the original GRPO. These results suggest that substantial training work can be saved by focusing updates on more informative completions and using the available hardware capacity more effectively.
neurips-2025-cppo-accelerating-the-train.tldr: CPPO accelerates GRPO training by pruning completions with weak learning signals and dynamically allocating work across questions.

paragraphs: Curvature Tuning changes a pretrained model through its activation functions. The method introduces a single adjustable parameter that steers the shape of the model's decision boundary, the boundary separating its predictions. This provides an interpretable way to alter behavior without requiring weight training, while also supporting a trainable version of the same parameter.

The authors analyze activation functions as spline operators and prove that the adjustment controls decision-boundary curvature. They also show that it projects the model into a space of smooth functions. This gives the parameter a mathematical interpretation and makes the method complementary to fine-tuning approaches that primarily adapt features. Learning the parameter produces a highly parameter-efficient fine-tuning method.

Experiments report improvements in generalization and robustness. Across 12 datasets, ResNet-50 and ResNet-152 improve over both linear probing and LoRA. The paper also reports large relative increases in robust accuracy on a RobustBench benchmark. These findings connect the theoretical control over smoothness with measured benefits, while distinguishing the training-free steering option from the version that learns its parameter.
neurips-2025-curvature-tuning-provable-t.tldr: Curvature Tuning steers decision-boundary smoothness through one activation parameter, with theoretical guarantees and reported generalization and robustness gains.

paragraphs: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, agents sharing a policy network can converge on similar behavior. This reduces exploration and can prevent the group from finding better cooperative strategies. Existing approaches encourage policy differences using Wasserstein distance, but the paper argues that similarity between policies can make this diversity signal ineffective.

Wasserstein Contrastive Diversity, or WCD, instead separates agents' trajectory distributions in a learned representation space. Its next-step prediction method uses Contrastive Predictive Coding to learn trajectory representations that are distinguishable. This representation-learning step matters because increasing a distance is useful only when that distance captures meaningful behavioral differences.

The framework also introduces a kernel-based computation method to make the distance calculation more efficient and extends the two-distribution formulation to accommodate multiple agents. Across the evaluated challenging multi-agent tasks, WCD outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods and improves exploration. The findings support treating representation quality, diversity measurement, and computational efficiency as connected parts of the same exploration problem.
neurips-2025-encouraging-metric-aware-di.tldr: WCD improves cooperative exploration by learning trajectory representations in which differences between agents can be measured and encouraged effectively.

paragraphs: Erasure of Language Memory, or ELM, addresses concept-level unlearning: reducing a language model's ability to generate material associated with selected concepts while retaining its broader abilities. Its central idea is to use the model's own classification capabilities to judge whether content relates to the knowledge being targeted.

ELM turns those judgments into distributions that guide the unlearning process. It then applies targeted low-rank updates to reduce generation probabilities for concept-specific content. The approach links the model's ability to recognize a concept with changes to its tendency to produce that concept, making its own assessments part of the mechanism for selective removal.

The authors evaluate erasure in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and literary domains. Modified models perform near chance on assessments of the targeted concepts, while preserving coherent generation and benchmark performance on unrelated tasks. They also show strong robustness to adversarial attacks in the reported evaluation. These findings provide evidence that targeted concept suppression can coexist with retained general capability, with the erasure claim grounded in the assessments and attacks tested.
neurips-2025-erasing-conceptual-knowledg.tldr: ELM uses a language model's own concept judgments to guide targeted updates that suppress selected knowledge while preserving broader capabilities.

paragraphs: Federated learning can reduce computation and communication by freezing a pretrained backbone and training only a lightweight task head. The paper examines security risks in this setup, where poisoned client updates and backdoor attacks can undermine the shared model. FedRACE combines feature refinement with server-side detection to protect learning with partially frozen models.

Its first component, HStat-Net, turns frozen features into compact representations that are easier to separate with linear decision boundaries. Its second component, DevGuard, evaluates statistical deviations in clients' class-level predictions using generalized linear models. Adaptive thresholds informed by theoretical misclassification bounds and randomized majority voting are added to improve detection reliability.

The authors implement the framework on FedScale and evaluate it on CIFAR-100, Food-101, and Tiny ImageNet under multiple attack scenarios. They report a true positive rate reaching 99.3%, with a false positive rate below 1.2%, while maintaining model accuracy and improving generalization. The results support combining representation design and statistical screening when securing this particular form of federated fine-tuning.
neurips-2025-fedrace-a-hierarchical-and-.tldr: FedRACE combines feature refinement and statistical client screening to defend federated learning with partially frozen pretrained models.

paragraphs: Simulation-based inference uses scientific simulators to estimate uncertain parameters from observations. It has worked best when those parameters form a small collection of numbers. Many scientific problems instead require inferring an entire function, such as a quantity varying across space or time, which makes the inference problem substantially more demanding.

FNOPE addresses this setting by combining a Fourier Neural Operator architecture with a flow matching objective for posterior estimation. The posterior represents uncertainty about parameters after accounting for observations. The method supports function-valued parameters and can estimate vector-valued parameters at the same time, allowing these two forms of unknown quantities to be handled together.

The authors report that FNOPE performs function-valued inference using a fraction of the simulations required by state-of-the-art methods. It also supports posterior evaluation at arbitrary discretizations of the domain, providing flexibility in how functions are represented for evaluation. Tests on benchmark problems and a challenging spatial glaciology task demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and its potential to broaden scientific applications of simulation-based inference.
neurips-2025-fnope-simulation-based-infe.tldr: FNOPE combines Fourier Neural Operators and flow matching to infer uncertain functions efficiently from scientific simulations.

paragraphs: Graph kernels compare graphs by measuring their similarity, but many use a fixed comparison rule that cannot be directly adjusted for the prediction task. The paper introduces Hierarchical Shortest-Path Graph Kernel Network, or HSP-GKN, to connect graph similarity estimation with task-specific learning in one optimization framework.

The method first transforms a graph into hierarchical features using a shortest-path kernel designed to preserve semantic and structural information. It then compares those features with learnable hidden graph features. The resulting collection of similarity scores becomes the graph embedding used by the neural network, so similarity is part of the representation supplied to the downstream task.

End-to-end training allows the framework to learn task-specific representations through these comparisons. This matters because the graph distinctions useful for one objective may differ from those useful for another. The authors report extensive experiments in which both the kernel and the learning framework outperform current competitors. The contribution is therefore a combination of hierarchical graph description and a trainable mechanism for turning graph comparisons into useful predictions.
neurips-2025-hierarchical-shortest-path-.tldr: HSP-GKN combines hierarchical shortest-path features with learnable graph comparisons to produce task-specific graph representations.

paragraphs: This paper revisits the claim that convolutional neural networks inherently favor texture over shape. The authors identify limitations in experiments that force a choice between conflicting visual cues. They introduce a domain-agnostic evaluation framework that systematically suppresses shape, texture, and color, allowing feature reliance to be examined under controlled conditions.

Evaluating humans and neural networks with this framework, the authors find that the tested CNNs predominantly rely on local shape features. Their results challenge the interpretation of these networks as inherently texture-biased. They also find that modern training strategies or architectures, including ConvNeXt and vision transformers, can substantially reduce this local-shape reliance.

Extending the evaluation across application domains reveals different patterns. Computer vision models emphasize shape, medical imaging models emphasize color, and remote sensing models rely more strongly on texture. These findings make feature reliance a property to measure in relation to training, architecture, and domain. The methodological contribution is a controlled way to investigate those dependencies without relying on forced conflicts between cues.
neurips-2025-imagenet-trained-cnns-are-n.tldr: Controlled cue suppression challenges inherent CNN texture bias and reveals feature reliance that varies with architecture, training, and application domain.

paragraphs: Craig interpolants are logical statements used in formal verification, including model checking, invariant generation, and abstraction refinement. For linear integer arithmetic, they help derive invariants describing safe or unreachable program states. The paper focuses on making these statements simpler and easier to interpret, addressing a difficulty that remains even when existing algorithms can generate valid interpolants.

The proposed approach uses a lightweight learned model to guide the process. The model learns to sample input problems lazily and works alongside established logical methods. In this setup, learning supplies guidance while the existing solver continues producing interpolants, connecting a learned sampling strategy with a formal reasoning procedure.

When the learned model guides Z3, the authors report reductions in interpolant complexity of up to 47.3%. For older solvers, reductions reach up to 69.1%. These are reported maximum improvements rather than uniform gains. The results show that learned guidance can help existing interpolation tools produce more concise logical statements, supporting the paper's goal of more interpretable formal verification.
neurips-2025-learning-simple-interpolant.tldr: A lightweight learned sampling model guides existing solvers toward simpler interpolants for linear integer arithmetic.

paragraphs: Standard vision-transformer attention compares every pair of tokens, including pairs with weak or redundant visual relationships. Visual-Contrast Attention, or VCA, replaces this operation with a mechanism that explicitly emphasizes differences between regions. It reduces theoretical complexity from quadratic token interactions to interactions involving a much smaller set of contrast tokens.

VCA spatially pools each attention head's query field into a few representative tokens. These feed learnable positive and negative streams whose differential interaction highlights distinguishing visual information. On DeiT-Tiny, the module adds fewer than 0.3 million parameters and requires no extra FLOPs. The authors present it as an architecture-agnostic replacement for multi-head self-attention.

Experiments raise DeiT-Tiny ImageNet-1K accuracy from 72.2% to 75.6%, with gains also reported for hierarchical vision transformers. Image-generation experiments improve FID-50K across diffusion and flow models. Ablations attribute benefits to pooled global cues and dual positional embeddings, with their combination performing best. Together, the results support using explicit visual contrast to improve both recognition and generation.
neurips-2025-linear-differential-vision-.tldr: Visual-Contrast Attention uses pooled tokens and differential interactions to improve vision-transformer recognition and generation with lower theoretical attention complexity.

paragraphs: The paper studies representation learning in an anti-causal setting, where labels cause observed features. Its goal is to learn representations that remain useful when the environment changes. Anti-Causal Invariant Abstractions, or ACIA, provides a measure-theoretic framework for separating how observations are generated from the stable patterns that support predictions across environments.

ACIA uses two representation levels. The lower level captures how labels generate observations, while the higher level captures causal patterns that persist through environment-specific variation. Interventional kernels allow the framework to accommodate both perfect and imperfect interventions. The approach also avoids requiring an explicit causal structure and is designed to handle high-dimensional data.

The theoretical results provide guarantees for out-of-distribution generalization and tight bounds on performance differences between training and unseen environments. Experiments on synthetic data and real-world medical datasets report better accuracy and invariance than state-of-the-art methods. These findings support the two-level design within the anti-causal setting studied, connecting stable representations with both formal analysis and empirical performance.
neurips-2025-measure-theoretic-anti-caus.tldr: ACIA learns two levels of anti-causal representations to capture observation generation and stable patterns across changing environments.

paragraphs: Counting which groups appear in generated text can miss differences in how those groups are described. This paper develops GAS(P), an evaluation method for detecting group-level representational biases across distributions of generated text. It focuses on an unprompted setting, where the input does not specify which societal groups should appear.

The authors apply the method to gendered descriptions of occupations in biographies and personas generated by state-of-the-art language models. Although generated biographies include a large representation of women, statistically significant differences remain in the words used to describe different genders across occupations. The analysis connects many of these differences with stereotypes and representational harms.

The findings show why increased numerical representation alone is an incomplete measure of progress. A group can appear frequently while repeatedly receiving stereotyped descriptions. The authors caution that simply increasing unprompted representation may also spread existing biases more widely. GAS(P) contributes a systematic way to examine these distribution-level differences, adding evidence about the character of representation to counts of who appears.
neurips-2025-more-of-the-same-persistent.tldr: GAS(P) reveals that greater representation of women in generated text can coexist with persistent gendered stereotypes in how people are described.

paragraphs: PartNeXt supports understanding 3D objects through their constituent parts. It contains more than 23,000 textured models across 50 categories, with detailed labels organized hierarchically. This structure represents parts at multiple levels of detail. The dataset addresses limitations associated with untextured geometry and annotation processes that depend heavily on experts.

The authors evaluate two forms of part understanding. Class-agnostic segmentation tests whether methods can separate object parts, and existing methods struggle with fine details and the smallest parts in the hierarchy. A new part-centric question-answering benchmark tests 3D language models and exposes gaps in connecting open-vocabulary descriptions to the corresponding object parts.

Training Point-SAM on PartNeXt produces substantial gains over training on PartNet, supporting the value of the new dataset's quality and diversity. By combining textures, hierarchical labels, scalable annotation, and multiple evaluation tasks, PartNeXt provides a resource for studying both geometric partitioning and language-based understanding. Its benchmarks also identify specific levels of part detail where current methods remain weak.
neurips-2025-partnext-a-next-generation-.tldr: PartNeXt provides textured 3D objects with hierarchical part labels and benchmarks that expose gaps in detailed segmentation and language-based part understanding.

paragraphs: Perception Encoder is a family of vision encoders for image and video understanding. The paper investigates whether contrastive vision-language training can produce representations useful across tasks that traditionally favor different pretraining objectives. After scaling a carefully tuned image-training recipe and refining it with a video data engine, the authors find broad capabilities within the resulting network.

The key qualification is where those capabilities appear: the useful general representations reside in intermediate layers. To make them available for downstream use, the authors introduce language alignment for multimodal language modeling and spatial alignment for dense prediction. These two methods adapt the internal visual information to the requirements of different task families.

The resulting models achieve reported state-of-the-art performance across classification, retrieval, question answering, detection, tracking, and depth estimation. This range includes both images and videos. The findings suggest that assessing a vision encoder only through its final output can overlook valuable internal representations. The release includes models, code, and a video dataset with synthetic and human annotations.
neurips-2025-perception-encoder-the-best.tldr: Perception Encoder extracts broadly useful intermediate visual representations through language and spatial alignment.

paragraphs: Reasoning models often generate long chains of thought, increasing the size of the key-value cache used during inference. Compressing that cache can reduce resource use, but existing compression approaches can also disrupt reasoning. R-KV addresses this problem by specifically targeting redundant tokens in reasoning models.

The reported results retain nearly all full-cache performance while using only 10% of the cache. Existing cache-compression baselines reach about 60% of full-cache performance in the stated comparison. With 38% of the cache, R-KV reaches 105% of the full-cache performance, showing that the tested compression setting can even improve the measured result.

The cache reduction also produces reported total memory savings of 50% and a twofold speedup over standard chain-of-thought inference. Those resource measurements are distinct from the percentage of cache retained. Across two mathematical reasoning datasets, R-KV consistently outperforms existing compression baselines. The findings support redundancy-aware cache management as a way to preserve reasoning quality while reducing the cost of long generations.
neurips-2025-r-kv-redundancy-aware-kv-ca.tldr: R-KV targets redundant reasoning tokens to shrink inference caches substantially while retaining nearly all full-cache performance in reported tests.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to estimate a discrete probability distribution when data are spread across terminals with limited communication. Each terminal holds multiple independent samples but can transmit only a restricted number of bits. Estimation error is measured using a family of losses indexed by p, allowing the analysis to cover different ways of weighting errors.

The authors develop refinement protocols that begin with a rough estimate obtained from partial information. Later steps use that estimate to guide more precise estimation. Depending on the parameter regime, the protocols combine successive refinement, sample compression, thresholding, and random hashing. The common principle is to use an initial approximation to direct the remaining limited communication.

The analysis establishes minimax-optimal error rates for most parameter regimes, supported by matching lower bounds on what any protocol can achieve. It also identifies an elbow at p = 2, where the behavior of the optimal rates changes. The contribution links practical protocol design with fundamental limits, while retaining the qualification that optimality covers most regimes rather than all of them.
neurips-2025-refinement-methods-for-dist.tldr: Refinement-based communication protocols achieve minimax-optimal distribution-estimation rates in most regimes and reveal a transition at p = 2.

paragraphs: Virtual screening searches chemical candidates for promising biological activity, but low hit rates and expensive computation make selection efficiency important. Active learning can guide which molecules to evaluate, yet fixed, handcrafted selection rules can struggle to balance chemical diversity and selection accuracy. GLARE replaces those inflexible heuristics with a learned selection policy.

The framework treats screening as a Markov decision process and trains its policy using Group Relative Policy Optimization. Its decisions dynamically balance chemical diversity, biological relevance, and computational constraints. This makes the selection strategy adaptable to the screening process, with the policy learning how to manage several competing considerations together.

Experiments report a 64.8% average improvement in enrichment factors over state-of-the-art active-learning methods. GLARE also improves screening foundation models such as DrugCLIP, with gains of up to eightfold in the reported EF at 0.5% measure using as few as 15 active molecules. These findings support adaptive molecule selection as a way to improve computational screening efficiency and the concentration of promising candidates.
neurips-2025-reinforced-active-learning-.tldr: GLARE learns an adaptive molecule-selection policy that improves virtual-screening enrichment while balancing diversity, relevance, and computational cost.

paragraphs: Earth observation foundation models can generalize across tasks, but that does not establish how well they handle corrupted inputs. REOBench evaluates this question using high-resolution optical remote sensing imagery. It covers six tasks and twelve corruption types, including changes to image appearance and geometry.

The benchmark compares models pretrained through masked image modeling, contrastive learning, and vision-language objectives. This design supports analysis across training approaches as well as architectures and backbone sizes. Its focus on high-resolution optical imagery connects the evaluation to applications such as urban planning and disaster response, where robustness is relevant to model reliability.

The results show significant degradation under corruption, with reported drops ranging from less than 1% to more than 25%. The size of the decline depends on the task, architecture, backbone size, and corruption type. Vision-language models show stronger robustness, particularly on multimodal tasks. These findings provide a more differentiated view of reliability than clean-input performance alone and identify factors associated with stronger or weaker resistance to input corruption.
neurips-2025-reobench-benchmarking-robus.tldr: REOBench finds substantial, task-dependent robustness gaps in Earth observation foundation models across twelve image corruption types.

paragraphs: Latent diffusion models can develop structural distortions when generating images above their training resolution. RepLDM addresses this by reprogramming a pretrained model for higher-resolution generation. The goal is to improve image quality and inference efficiency without relying on extensive retraining, addressing weaknesses reported for existing reprogramming methods.

The framework has two stages. First, attention guidance uses a parameter-free self-attention mechanism to produce a latent representation of a better, structurally consistent image at the training resolution. Second, progressive upsampling enlarges the image in pixel space. This choice is intended to reduce the severe artifacts associated with upsampling directly in latent space.

The first stage supplies an effective starting point, allowing higher-resolution denoising to use substantially fewer steps. The two stages therefore connect structural quality with computational efficiency: a better initial image supports a cheaper enlargement process. Extensive experiments report substantial quality and efficiency gains over state-of-the-art high-resolution generation methods, supporting this staged approach to extending pretrained models beyond their original training resolution.
neurips-2025-repldm-reprogramming-pretra.tldr: RepLDM combines attention-guided initialization with progressive pixel-space upsampling for higher-quality, more efficient high-resolution diffusion generation.

paragraphs: Learning from heart-ultrasound videos requires sensitivity to both subtle anatomy and changing motion. The paper identifies difficulties for existing self-supervised methods, including similar-looking samples, noisy ultrasound inputs, and augmentations that can distort clinically relevant information. DISCOVR addresses these issues with separate image and video branches that learn complementary representations.

The video branch uses clustering to model temporal dynamics. An image encoder learns fine-grained spatial meaning and continues evolving during training. A semantic cluster distillation loss transfers anatomical knowledge from this image encoder into the video encoder. This connects detailed spatial understanding with representations that remain coherent over time.

The authors evaluate DISCOVR on six echocardiography datasets covering fetal, pediatric, and adult populations. It outperforms specialized video anomaly-detection methods and state-of-the-art video self-supervised baselines in zero-shot and linear-probing evaluations. The paper also reports stronger segmentation transfer and downstream performance on tasks including left ventricular ejection fraction prediction. These results support transferring image-level anatomical information as a way to strengthen learned cardiac-video representations.
neurips-2025-self-supervised-learning-of.tldr: DISCOVR transfers anatomical information from an evolving image encoder into a video encoder to improve self-supervised heart-ultrasound representations.

paragraphs: Text-to-motion models need to produce movements that are realistic, consistent, and aligned with human preferences. This paper studies how preference-based fine-tuning can make high-quality motions more consistently favored. Its theoretical analysis identifies different weaknesses in direct preference optimization: offline training can overfit, while online training can suffer from biased sampling.

Semi-online Preference Optimization, or SoPo, builds each training pair from two sources. The preferred motion comes from an existing offline dataset, while the unpreferred motion comes from the online distribution. This pairing combines the two training settings so that each can compensate for the other's identified limitations.

Experiments on MLD and MDM report better performance than other preference-alignment methods. The MLD model fine-tuned with SoPo also exceeds the compared state-of-the-art model on R-precision and MM Dist, and visualizations provide additional evidence of preference alignment. The contribution is a specific way to construct preference pairs that connects theoretical concerns about data sourcing with measured improvements in text-to-motion generation.
neurips-2025-sopo-text-to-motion-generat.tldr: SoPo improves motion preference alignment by pairing preferred offline motions with unpreferred motions from the online distribution.

paragraphs: STRCMP is an algorithm-discovery framework for difficult combinatorial optimization problems. The paper argues that language-model approaches often overlook structural information inherent in these problems, reducing solution quality and making iterative search inefficient. Its approach explicitly incorporates graph structure when generating solver-specific algorithm code.

A graph neural network extracts structural embeddings from optimization instances. A language model conditions on these embeddings to generate candidate algorithms, connecting problem topology with natural-language objectives. The framework is designed to ensure syntactic correctness, preserve topology, and refine generated algorithms through an evolutionary process that iteratively searches for improved candidates.

The authors evaluate STRCMP on mixed integer linear programming and Boolean satisfiability problems across nine benchmark datasets. It outperforms five strong neural and language-model methods by a large margin in both solution optimality and computational efficiency. These results support giving code-generating language models explicit structural information about the problems they are solving. The contribution combines structural representation, code generation, and iterative algorithm refinement within one discovery framework.
neurips-2025-texttt-strcmp-integrating-g.tldr: STRCMP conditions language-model algorithm generation on graph structure and uses evolutionary refinement to improve combinatorial optimization.

paragraphs: Large reasoning models improve problem solving through long chains of thought, but longer generations make deployment more expensive. This paper studies how training can encourage models to use less unnecessary computation while keeping most of their accuracy. The objective is to make the reasoning process itself more efficient.

The proposed method incentivizes reduced computational overhead and exposes a single hyperparameter that controls efficiency. Adjusting it produces a family of reasoning models with different efficiency levels. This gives the training procedure a way to express how strongly it should prioritize reducing reasoning cost while seeking to preserve accuracy.

Experiments on two open-weight reasoning models show substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining most of the original accuracy. The stated result therefore allows some accuracy loss and concerns the models evaluated. Its practical significance is that deployment efficiency can be shaped during training, producing several operating points rather than a single fixed reasoning behavior. This directly addresses the costs associated with lengthy generated reasoning.
neurips-2025-training-language-models-to.tldr: An efficiency-focused training method reduces reasoning-model inference costs while preserving most accuracy, with one parameter controlling the tradeoff.
